title: Improve KV cache memory management and eviction policies to reduce fragmentation, paging, and spillover
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: production KV cache fragmentation and spillover have caused elevated memory peaks and unexpected paging under mixed multi-tenant workloads. This PR refactors the KV cache allocator and eviction policies to reduce fragmentation, introduce cooperative background compaction, and implement an async spillover pathway with backpressure. Approach: 1) replace the previous naive free-list allocator with a size-bucketed allocator that reduces internal fragmentation for common key/value sizes; 2) add a low-priority, cooperative compaction pass that coalesces small free regions when the cache is under memory pressure; 3) implement size-aware LRU eviction that prefers evicting large cold entries first and groups evictions into batches to avoid multiple small allocations; 4) add an async spillover mechanism that pages cold KV entries to an on-disk spill store (configurable path) and maintains lightweight in-memory stubs to avoid blocking the hot path; 5) instrument new metrics (kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache_compaction_runs, kv_cache_spill_io_ops, kv_cache_effective_capacity) and expose runtime knobs for aggressiveness and spill thresholds. Testing: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration tests with synthetic multi-tenant workloads, e2e benchmark harness comparing old vs new behavior. Benchmarks and results are summarized below. Rollout: feature gated behind kv_cache_v2 flag with canary on dedicated pools, 48 hour observation window, automatic rollback triggers defined. Backports: critical bugfix to spill store permission handling will be backported to the 2026.01 branch. See release_notes for user-visible changes and migration notes.

review_comments: Diego Morales: This looks promising — can you explain how compaction avoids stalling the hot path? Specifically, what guarantees ensure we don't introduce p95 regressions during a compaction window?

Ava Chen (author): Compaction is cooperative and yields after fixed byte quotas; it runs on a separate low-priority worker and only touches free regions and cold candidates identified by access time heuristics. Hot path access checks the in-memory stub and will trigger a fast promote if needed; we also added adaptive dial-down of compaction when p95 increases are observed.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management and eviction policies: reduced fragmentation via size-bucketed allocator and cooperative compaction; size-aware LRU eviction to prefer large cold entries; async spillover to disk for cold KV entries; new metrics and runtime knobs. Backwards-compatible default behavior is unchanged; enable kv_cache_v2 to opt into new allocator. Operators should monitor kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio and kv_cache_spill_io_ops after rollout.
benchmark_summary: Synthetic multi-tenant benchmark: p95 token-append latency reduced 12-18% under mixed workloads, peak RSS reduced ~28% for workloads with many variable-size KV entries, effective cache capacity increased by 6-9% due to lower fragmentation, cold-entry eviction throughput improved ~2x, spillover IO added <2% tail latency when active; overall cost per token reduced for large context workloads in Dedicated pools.
rollout_plan: Gate behind kv_cache_v2 flag; canary on 5% of Dedicated pools for 48h; monitor kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio, p95 latency, error rate; rollback triggers: error rate >0.5% absolute or p95 increases >5% for 10 minutes. Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days if stable.
notes: Backported critical permissions fix to 2026.01 branch; operator docs updated; test harness added for reproducing fragmentation pattern.
